title: PRD: map incident severity to rollout gates and synthetic verification harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After the recent multi-region KV-cache stall postmortem, product needs to codify a concrete mapping from incident severity to automated rollout gates and a synthetic verification harness that validates those gates during canary and progressive rollouts. This PRD update translates action items from the incident runbook into shippable requirements: precise gate conditions, ownerable checks, acceptance tests, and rollback thresholds.

Goals: 1) Ensure all runtime rollouts have clearly defined severity-to-gate mappings (what constitutes immediate rollback vs degraded mode). 2) Provide a repeatable synthetic verification harness that runs pre-rollout and continuous post-rollout checks for common failure modes (KV cache stalls, coldstart tail-latency spikes, kernel regression). 3) Surface operator-visible signals and playbook links in Console to reduce mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-recover.

Scope: Product and SRE-owned PRD additions for the runtime rollout flow. Scope includes: gate definitions, synthetic check scenarios, canary pass/fail thresholds, monitoring dashboards and alerts, runbook links, and acceptance criteria for release. This does NOT include implementing the runtime failure mitigation code (ENG tickets referenced).

Out of scope: new kernel or quantization work, pricing changes, or enterprise contract updates.

Context and rationale: The postmortem found unclear thresholds and ambiguous rollback criteria led to delayed rollbacks and a larger blast radius. Engineering already has prototype failure detectors (ENG-58821) and a dashboard spike detector (ENG-59220). Product must make these operationally actionable and testable in release pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: A1: For each incident severity level (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) there is an explicit rollout gate definition: metric, window, threshold, and action (block, degrade, rollback).

A2: The synthetic verification harness implements at least 5 scenarios: KV cache stall, coldstart tail latency, long-tail OOMs on batch, kernel mis-compiled step, and serving-endpoint 5xx spike; each scenario has a deterministic pass/fail signal.

A3: Canary policy must include automated decisions: if >0.5% requests exceed tail-latency threshold for 10m OR error_rate > 0.2% for 5m -> fail and rollback to previous model/version. Thresholds configurable per release channel.
A4: Runbook links and a one-click rollback in Console are surfaced for all runtime rollouts and tested in a dry-run (no-traffic) exercise.
A5: Operator dashboard displays the active gate state, time-since-canary-start, and the top 3 contributing metrics to the gate decision; synthetic harness results are retained for 30 days.
A6: Integration tests in CI (release pipeline) exercise the synthetic harness and must pass before a staged rollout proceeds to production (green CI signal required).
A7: Post-release automated verification runs at 1m, 5m, 15m and 1h intervals and will auto-open an incident if gate violation persists for configured durations.
verification_steps: Step 1: Review gate matrix and sign off (PM + SRE + ENG). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/prd/runtime-rollout-gates
Step 2: Wire synthetic harness into pre-release pipeline (ENG-58821), run harness in no-traffic mode and validate deterministic failures are detected.
Step 3: Execute a controlled canary with synthetic fault injection in staging; verify automatic rollback triggers within the configured thresholds.
Step 4: Confirm Console dashboard shows gate status and runbook link; runbook contains operator steps and escalation path.
Step 5: Post-release: validate scheduled synthetic checks and ensure alerts create an incident ticket template automatically.
Step 6: Conduct a retrospective after the first production rollout and capture any new failure modes for PRD update.
decisions: Decision 1: Severity mapping will be SEV1->immediate rollback, SEV2->degrade with operator approval after automated mitigation attempts, SEV3->monitor and require manual review before rollout continues.
Decision 2: Canary thresholds chosen to prioritize user-visible latency and correctness over marginal cost increases (tail-latency SLOs override throughput cost targets during canary).
Decision 3: Synthetic harness will be open-sourced internally to allow ENG teams to add new scenarios tied to PRs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives in synthetic checks causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: tune thresholds in staging using historical incident data and provide hysteresis window before rollback.
Risk: Increased release latency due to additional verification steps. Mitigation: parallelize harness runs and allow opt-out flags for urgent hotfixes with SRE approval.
communication_plan: Send announcement to #product-runtime and #sre with PRD links and rollout timeline.
Schedule a 30m working session with Eng and SRE to align on CI gating changes (invite ENG-58821 owner).
Update release checklist and include sign-off step for gate matrix owners.
impact_summary: This PRD update reduces ambiguity in rollout decisions, shortens detection-to-rollback time for severe incidents, and creates a repeatable verification surface to prevent regressions that caused the previous outage. Expected benefit: 30-50% reduction in time-to-rollback for SEV1-type regressions; measurable reduction in post-release incident volume after 2 releases.
notes: Follow-up: incorporate post-rollout telemetry tagging so incident automation can map back to PR/commit.
Owner: Riley Chen (PM) — coordinate with SRE lead Mateo Alvarez and ENG owners listed in dependencies.
